feedback.answered: The client-side half of the codec finding's applicability is answered: the client caps nothing. Its loop allocates one buffer of exactly the configured command size (make([]byte, c.psize) with psize taken from config.CommandSize) and fills it with random bytes, and every write sends that whole buffer as the command value, with no length check anywhere on the path. So the applicability of claim C10 is not hypothetical: a deployment that configures values larger than the 65535-byte length field makes every write an oversized command, which the three confirmed scenarios show ends in a truncated value, a corrupted following command, and a receiver-side decode panic. The shipped aws.conf's 1000-byte setting is what keeps the default deployment inside the field's range.
